# Proteomics {#sec-proteomics}

::: {.callout-note title="From the exam description"}
Different proteomics methods. How are these used, algorithms.
:::

## Introduction

::: {.callout-warning title="To be written"}
Short introduction: mass-spectrometry-based proteomics — from proteins to
peptides to spectra; identifying peptides by database search; controlling
errors with target–decoy strategies; quantification; and complementary
antibody- and affinity-based methods.
:::

## Key concepts

- Bottom-up (shotgun) vs. top-down proteomics; LC-MS/MS; fragmentation and b/y ions
- Peptide identification: database search (SEQUEST, Mascot, Andromeda), spectral libraries, de novo sequencing
- Error control: target–decoy approach, peptide-spectrum-match FDR, Percolator; the protein inference problem
- Acquisition strategies: data-dependent (DDA) vs. data-independent (DIA/SWATH) vs. targeted (SRM/PRM)
- Quantification: label-free, SILAC, isobaric tags (TMT/iTRAQ)
- Post-translational modifications (e.g. phosphoproteomics)
- Interaction proteomics (AP-MS, cross-linking MS; see @sec-protein-interactions) and structural MS
- Deep learning for spectrum and retention-time prediction
- Antibody-based proteomics: the Human Protein Atlas
- Repositories and standards: PRIDE/ProteomeXchange

## Key papers

### Reviews — start here

- @aebersold2003 — mass spectrometry-based proteomics.
- @aebersold2016 — mass-spectrometric exploration of proteome structure and function.
- @nesvizhskii2010 — computational methods and error-rate estimation for peptide and protein identification.
- @ludwig2018 — data-independent acquisition-based proteomics: a tutorial.

### Identification and error control

- @eng1994 — SEQUEST: matching spectra to sequences.
- @perkins1999 — Mascot: probability-based protein identification.
- @elias2007 — the target–decoy search strategy.
- @kall2007 — Percolator: semi-supervised learning for peptide identification.

### Quantification and acquisition

- @cox2008 — MaxQuant.
- @gillet2012 — SWATH-MS.
- @demichev2020 — DIA-NN: neural networks for DIA data.
- @gessulat2019 — Prosit: deep-learning prediction of fragment spectra.

### Proteome maps and resources

- @kim2014 — a draft map of the human proteome.
- @wilhelm2014 — mass-spectrometry-based draft of the human proteome.
- @uhlen2015 — the tissue-based map of the human proteome (Human Protein Atlas).
- @perezriverol2022 — the PRIDE database.
- @ideker2001 — integrated genomic and proteomic analysis of a perturbed network.
